Risk title: Investment in fleet capacity that does not match future demand
Value effects: Organic EBITDA; Investment EBITDA; Multiple; Cash/NIBD
Cause: OUTCOME DRIVERS (market/context): uncertain salmon production, customer demand and competitor capacity forecasts. TRIDENT-SIDE FAILURE MODES (actionable): (1) investment case built on a single demand scenario without downside bands; (2) segment/geo capacity commits ahead of validated orderbook or utilization evidence; (3) competitor delivery pipeline not refreshed into the fleet plan; (4) no stage-gate linking forecast refresh to Capex go/no-go; (5) Finance/Commercial/Ops assumptions not reconciled before FID.
Risk event: Trident commits capital to vessel segments or geographies with insufficient demand
Consequences: Low utilization, reduced returns and constrained financial flexibility
Current mitigation: S&BD+Finance: (1) maintain a multi-scenario demand and competitor-capacity pack for each Capex case; (2) require orderbook/utilization evidence thresholds before capacity commit; (3) quarterly refresh of competitor delivery pipeline into the fleet plan; (4) stage-gate Capex decisions to the latest forecast cycle (SBD-P02/P04/P06); (5) cross-functional assumption sign-off (S&BD, Commercial, Ops, Finance) before FID.
Evidence / rationale: Illustrative – validate

Risk title: Contract renewals fail to deliver planned rate uplift
Cause: OUTCOME DRIVERS (market): tender pressure, soft utilization, customer resistance to re-pricing toward newbuild parity. TRIDENT-SIDE FAILURE MODES (actionable): (1) renewal calendar without a per-contract rate/terms mandate (corridor, indexation, duration); (2) weak comps / newbuild-parity pack for negotiators before talks open; (3) no clear BATNA (redeploy, idle, or other region), so soft rates get accepted; (4) late escalation when the renewal forecast slips versus the uplift plan; (5) term-playbook not applied in negotiation (indexation, tenor, off-hire, signing gates).
Risk event: Material renewals close at rates below the organic rate-uplift plan.
Consequences: Like-for-like EBITDA and cash generation undershoot the value-creation plan.
Current mitigation: S&BD+Commercial: (1) keep a 12-24 month renewal calendar with target TC rate, indexation, and duration per material contract; (2) require a pre-negotiation brief (comps, customer alternatives, BATNA) before talks open; (3) set a formal rate/terms mandate from CCO/S&BD and a deal-review gate before signing below corridor; (4) run a monthly renewal gap versus plan with escalation when below corridor; (5) link the SBD-P05 operating agenda to each material renewal (mandate, gap, escalate, feed back).
Evidence / rationale: Operationalized for S&BD: outcome risk broken into Trident controllable failure modes and mitigations — validate with Commercial.

TRIDENT-SIDE FAILURE MODES (actionable): (1) orderbook and competitor delivery watch not tied to Trident utilization forecasts; (2) new awards pursued without testing dilution on the existing fleet; (3) no early trigger when segment utilization or rate softens versus plan; (4) segment mix bets not revisited when oversupply signals appear; (5) Commercial incentives favor volume over protecting existing utilization.
Risk event: Paid utilization and off-hire performance on existing vessels deteriorate below plan.
Consequences: Organic EBITDA, contract quality optics, and near-term cash conversion weaken.
Current mitigation: S&BD+Commercial: (1) maintain a segment orderbook/delivery watch linked to utilization forecast; (2) require an existing-fleet dilution test before pursuing material new awards; (3) set utilization/rate soft-landing triggers with escalation to SBD-P02/P05; (4) revisit segment mix bets when oversupply signals breach threshold; (5) weight Commercial scorecards to protect core fleet utilization, not only new volume.

Risk title: Commercial terms erode (indexation, pass-through, duration)
Cause: OUTCOME DRIVERS (market/context): customers push back on CPI indexation, fuel pass-through, or multi-year tenure. TRIDENT-SIDE FAILURE MODES (actionable): (1) term-playbook not loaded into renewal/new-award mandates; (2) negotiators concede indexation or pass-through without a priced trade; (3) short tenor accepted without premium or exit rights; (4) no deal-review gate when core terms fall below playbook minimums; (5) lost-term patterns not fed back into the next negotiation cycle.
Risk event: New and renewed contracts carry weaker economic protections than the operating agenda assumes.
Consequences: Margin compression and higher earnings volatility reduce organic EBITDA quality.
Current mitigation: S&BD+Commercial: (1) load term-playbook minimums (indexation, pass-through, tenor) into every material mandate; (2) require a priced trade for any concession on indexation or pass-through; (3) accept short tenor only with premium and/or Trident exit rights; (4) deal-review gate before signing below playbook minimums; (5) capture lost-term patterns into the next SBD-P05 negotiation cycle.

Risk title: Fleet redeployment misses higher-return regional demand
Cause: OUTCOME DRIVERS (market/context): regional willingness-to-pay and demand differ; tonnage can remain in lower-return regions while another region (e.g. Chile) is short. TRIDENT-SIDE FAILURE MODES (actionable): (1) market intel not turned into a timed portfolio case (demand evidence, vessel fit, constraints); (2) treating inter-region moves as liquid — ignoring reconstruction, yard slot, transit, flag/class/biosecurity, and commercial exit costs; (3) no ranked options with full economics (move / wait / serve another way) and weak-region exit constraints not mapped early; (4) slow S&BD–Commercial–Ops decision rights so the Chile window closes, or no trigger when regional EBITDA/rate-utilization spread vs plan breaches threshold; (5) Chile (or destination) cannibalisation ignored — stronger incoming vessel can idle or reprice less competitive tonnage already in region.
Risk event: Vessels remain under-monetized relative to achievable regional rate and utilization differentials.
Consequences: Organic EBITDA growth lags peers and the platform's global flexibility advantage is underused.
Current mitigation: S&BD-led portfolio case (not a liquid move): (1) quarterly regional rate/utilization/EBITDA heat map vs P05 plan with a breach trigger to open a redeployment case (owner + decision deadline; do not auto-move); (2) ranked shortlist with vessel fit PLUS reconstruction scope/cost/time, transit and regulatory path, and exit/novation costs in the weak region; (3) destination impact pack: expected cannibalisation on existing Chile (or other) vessels — utilization, rate, residual value; (4) decision forum S&BD-Commercial-Ops: approve move / wait / alternative only if net fleet EBITDA after transaction costs and cannibalisation clears the hurdle (SBD-P02/P05/P06); (5) document rejected moves so the same weak case is not endlessly reopened.
Evidence / rationale: Operationalized: focus on decision speed and intel-to-action, not only market geography — validate.

Risk title: Underlying salmon supply growth undershoots consensus
Cause: OUTCOME DRIVERS (market/context): regulatory caps, biological setbacks, or slower farmer efficiency cut sea-based production growth below plan. TRIDENT-SIDE FAILURE MODES (actionable): (1) capacity and commercial plans locked to consensus growth without downside bands; (2) regional biology/regulatory signals not escalated into S&BD planning; (3) no early reforecast when farmer production guidance softens; (4) vessel pipeline and hiring not flexed when supply undershoots; (5) strategy narrative keeps assuming consensus growth after evidence turns.

Consequences: Utilization and rate momentum soften, pressuring organic EBITDA and delaying investment cases.
Current mitigation: S&BD: (1) hold downside and base supply scenarios in the fleet/commercial plan; (2) route regional biology and regulatory signals into SBD-P02/P01/P09 on a fixed cadence; (3) trigger reforecast when farmer guidance or harvest indicators soften; (4) flex vessel pipeline and crewing plans when supply undershoots consensus; (5) update the growth narrative and Capex gates when consensus is no longer evidence-based.
